variants.query: A servant stole property from their employer. What section may apply?

original.text: Whoever, being a clerk or servant, or being employed in the capacity of a clerk or servant, commits theft in respect of any property in the possession of his master or employer, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. Theft after preparation made for causing death, hurt or restraint in order to committing of theft.
original.derived_context:
Act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Chapter 17: OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY
Section 306: Theft by clerk or servant of property in possession of master.
Whoever, being a clerk or servant, or being employed in the capacity of a clerk or servant, commits theft in respect of any property in the possession of his master or employer, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. Theft after preparation made for causing death, hurt or restraint in order to committing of theft.

original.text: A being Z’s servant, and entrusted by Z with the care of Z’s plate, dishonestly runs away with the plate, without Z’s consent. A has committed theft.
original.derived_context:
Act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Chapter 17: OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY
Section 303: Theft.
Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person’s consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft.
A being Z’s servant, and entrusted by Z with the care of Z’s plate, dishonestly runs away with the plate, without Z’s consent. A has committed theft.

original.text: Property, the possession whereof has been transferred by theft or extortion or robbery or cheating, and property which has been criminally misappropriated or in respect of which criminal breach of trust has been committed, is designated as stolen property, whether the transfer has been made, or the misappropriation or breach of trust has been committed, within or without India, but, if such property subsequently comes into the possession of a person legally entitled to the possession thereof, it then ceases to be stolen property.
original.derived_context:
Act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Chapter 17: OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY
Section 317: Stolen property.
Property, the possession whereof has been transferred by theft or extortion or robbery or cheating, and property which has been criminally misappropriated or in respect of which criminal breach of trust has been committed, is designated as stolen property, whether the transfer has been made, or the misappropriation or breach of trust has been committed, within or without India, but, if such property subsequently comes into the possession of a person legally entitled to the possession thereof, it then ceases to be stolen property.

original.text: The consent mentioned in this section may be express or implied, and may be given either by the person in possession, or by any person having for that purpose authority either express or implied.
original.derived_context:
Act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Chapter 17: OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY
Section 303: Theft.
Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person’s consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft.
The consent mentioned in this section may be express or implied, and may be given either by the person in possession, or by any person having for that purpose authority either express or implied.

original.text: Whoever, being a clerk or servant or employed as a clerk or servant, and being in any manner entrusted in such capacity with property, or with any dominion over property, commits criminal breach of trust in respect of that property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
original.derived_context:
Act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Chapter 17: OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY
Section 316: Criminal breach of trust.
Whoever, being a clerk or servant or employed as a clerk or servant, and being in any manner entrusted in such capacity with property, or with any dominion over property, commits criminal breach of trust in respect of that property, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

original.text: Whoever dishonestly receives or retains any stolen property, the possession whereof he knows or has reason to believe to have been transferred by the commission of dacoity, or dishonestly receives from a person, whom he knows or has reason to believe to belong or to have belonged to a gang of dacoits, property which he knows or has reason to believe to have been stolen, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

phase11.summary_answer: Section 306 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 may apply to a servant who steals property from their employer.
phase11.detailed_answer: According to Section 306 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, a clerk or servant who commits theft of property in the possession of their master or employer is subject to punishment, which may include imprisonment for up to seven years and a fine. This section specifically addresses the scenario where a servant steals from their employer, making it applicable in such cases.
